change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: Displayed website name goes stale after editing the website
findings.body: The name was a computed property on `model.website`, so it updated when the user edited it in preferences (preferences.hbs:158 binds `model.website`). It is now a server-computed `website_name`. `save` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response (line 210), so after saving a new website the profile header keeps showing the old `website_name` (or nothing) until the user is reloaded. I did not check whether the route refetches the model. If it doesn't, copy `website_name` from the PUT response, which would need the update action to return it, or compute it client-side again.

findings.title: website_name is fragile and repeats work
findings.body: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal, which breaks under frozen string literals. `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three times. The `rescue nil` modifier hides every error. For `http://example.com/` the same-host branch returns `example.com/` with a trailing slash. The old client code kept the port (`split('/')[2]`) and this drops it. Parse once into a local, and use `"." + website_host` or `end_with?`.

findings.title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), but `website_name`, which is derived from it, is not. Is that intentional? Check what untrusted_attributes does for low-trust users.

findings.title: Missing coverage for sibling-subdomain branch and edge cases
findings.body: The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (serializer line 144) has no test. Neither do a website without a scheme (host nil, so no name is shown) or a website with a port. Add cases for these.

contracts.action: Profile header shows website name from server-provided website_name instead of controller computed websiteName
contracts.before_after: Before: derived client-side from model.website, so it was live. After: serializer-computed once at load, and shows the host (or host+path on same-site) only.
contracts.visible_effect: Header text next to the globe icon
contracts.failure_mode: After editing the website in preferences, save() does not refresh website_name, so the header can show a stale value
contracts.open_question: Does the user route refetch the model after preferences save?

summary: The change moves the website display name from the client to UserSerializer. The main risk is that `website_name` is not refreshed after the user edits their website, so the profile header can show a stale name. Minor points: the serializer code is fragile and repeats work, and the specs miss the sibling-subdomain branch and edge cases.
